context: E06 only; all complete reports read before source edits

findings.title: Reject invalid launch edits instead of substituting a truncated ID
findings.impact: A native profile launch can apply a different advertised model/mode/effort identity from the invalid value supplied by the user, bypassing the intended explicit rejection before startup settings are applied.
findings.evidence: Event::Paste calls Dialog::append, whose lines 179–183 remove control characters and stop appending at the byte limit, then clear the error. For an advertised valid 256-byte model ID M, pasting M followed by another byte stores only M. Dialog::request submits that substituted value; tui.rs routes it through NativeControl::launch, daemon profile preparation validates the already-rewritten string, and Configuration::resolve/next dispatches the genuine setter for M. The supplied 257-byte identity would otherwise fail valid_id. PLAN lines 17–23 requires exact advertised identities and explicit unsupported-setting failure, not silent model substitution. The file is new relative to base 2195b05adf23ae26a80065ecdd6d9196e2915998, confirmed by git show reporting it absent from that base.
findings.fix: Validate the complete proposed edit before mutating the backing field. Reject over-budget scalar/Options JSON edits in full with a visible error rather than keeping a prefix; reject control-containing scalar setting IDs rather than rewriting them. Preserve legal JSON bytes for the existing parser. Ensure rejected input cannot silently produce a launch, and add a native dialog regression using an offered 256-byte ID and an invalid 257-byte ID sharing that prefix.
